src/engine/task.hpp.reason: Complete API mixes semantic task ownership with source-slot graph interchange, fixture-default availability and instruction-boundary diagnostics; keep actual scheduler behavior in engine while extracting reference facts.
src/engine/task.hpp.semantic_justification: Task handles own resources; private links are nonowning and slot generations are explicit. optional slot/link/default values distinguish host tasks, null pointers and missing fixture observations. Declared lifecycle stages retain partial cleanup, not an imagined transaction rollback.

resolved_owners.resolution: TaskScheduler owns storage_, source_slots_, free_slots_, heads_, TaskContext, one shared arena/pool reservation and an explicit callback-context table. Task links are nonowning pointers into retained storage. WalkGuard defers scheduler reclamation through outermost native traversal; caller/cursor/graph handles can retain retired storage. Task owns allocation handles and canonical primary_state/motion_state/auxiliary_native_work; typed payloads are not byte-vector pose replicas. TaskResult/continuation handles retain partial cleanup state. ObjectControl linkage may hold a task until cleanup clears it; no second scheduler or GLOBAL is added.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Actual native LogoScene constructs/replaces the arena and scheduler; TitleScene registers explicit scene contexts, creates tasks, executes/displays/deletes them, and menu/preview callbacks borrow task work. Music manager destruction can clear the canonical handle used as destroy_task argument. NativeGame reference reset constructs the same scheduler and installs player child copying. HLE TaskBridge separately owns guest transport, imports/exports pool graphs and resumes guest callbacks. Unit/probe consumers exercise host append, source allocation, graph mutation, continuation and cleanup; none makes arbitrary native actor callbacks complete.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: Current-source native regression specifications: allocation/child/raw/live copy, pool exhaustion, saved-next mutation/reuse, explicit default-null versus unknown, partial cleanup/resume, auxiliary release ordering, canonical-owner destructor reset/replacement and graph motion identity. The historical gate pins current task/task_work files; Main music replay separately records task_callback_lifetime exit 0.
accepted_judges.limits: Accepted as bounded existing regression evidence, not a fresh execution or full original/hardware lifecycle proof.

src/engine/task_work.hpp.reason: Functional allocator/reference ownership is combined with reference_base, serialized-byte knownness and transport callbacks in the public engine contract. Separate these responsibilities without relocating recovered allocator behavior.
src/engine/task_work.hpp.semantic_justification: Free/physical links are optional offsets (offset0 is real), not host/guest pointers. TaskWork handles identify allocation generations. Interior reference results carry target allocation, byte offset and allocation-data provenance; whole-allocation access explicitly rejects interiors. Weak references prevent self-retention.

resolved_owners.resolution: TaskWorkArena owns backing bytes/knownness, physical/free block topology, live allocation handles and weak reference bindings. TaskWork carries raw owner identity/header/request/released state plus an optional typed collision payload. A handle is distinct from its reused numerical data offset. References record target allocation plus interior byte offset and original allocation_data_offset; weak targets do not retain themselves. Explicit release invalidates a retained handle independently of shared_ptr lifetime. No TaskWork method dereferences its raw owner after arena destruction; clients must keep the arena alive for operations.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Native scheduler creation/destruction, player initialization, collision cleanup, Gamma cursor generation and animation buffers consume the allocator. Startup publishes player+312 -> same allocation+56 and player+316 -> same allocation+0. Animation scalar consumption checks reference_view live and reads canonical physics speed/charge, never a copied byte scalar. Legacy Sonic motion binding resolves exact allocation identity through PlayerStartupRegistry; Native Gamma uses Registry.allocations. HLE alone installs base-address serialization and payload/resolver callbacks; its resolver currently resolves exact allocation bases, not arbitrary interiors.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: Current unit specifies first fit, rounded padding, preserved stale payload/header bytes, coalescing, exact fit/sentinel, wrap/exhaustion, released/foreign work, typed null/self/interior references, weak target lifetime, unknown pointer provenance and live payload callbacks. Current historical gate fingerprints both source files and runs task-work.
accepted_judges.limits: No new run. Unit contracts distinguish functional null links and unavailable serialized bytes; do not establish hardware heap acquisition or every failure/reentrant callback path.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: Historical allocator comparison reports exact return/head/full-arena bytes; current tracked summary cuts sequences to 10 of 16. accepted_judges.limits: Historical mutation receipts fingerprint older task/bridge/header sources; current task_work.cpp alone matches later lifetime evidence. No current complete mutation/holdout receipt or locally available frozen raw cases. Do not sum truncated lists into full corpus totals.

src/runtime/native_player_system.hpp.semantic_justification: Entire50-line header reviewed, including GammaExtraWork, PlayerSystem, resource binder declaration and Gamma Context. Context references remain invocation-local. Stage/act and callback values are supplied by actual callers; texture service pointers borrow local synchronous objects. deque preserves element references on current push_back use; it does not prove later erase/destructor behavior. Imported Gamma table still exposes legacy animation fixture-knownness through a separate contract already marked migration.

resolved_owners.resolution: Session embeds PlayerSystem before LogoScene and after CharacterPack/SceneState. It groups current publications, native registration/allocation records, Gamma source globals, one mutable GammaWeldInfo table, shared scene-backed cursor templates, deque elements tied to actual 580-byte E102WK allocations, and uniquely owned imported Gamma assets. Initialized player physics lives in Registry.allocations records and aliases task primary/motion owners; GammaExtraWork is separate from the 480-byte player auxiliary allocation. Join-table/geometry/template pointers are live borrows, not per-actor copies.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Native PreviewServices creates actual actor tasks and zero-backed typed primary/motion owners; Gamma callback forms invocation-local Context borrowing PlayerSystem/scheduler/bootstrap/rendering/task/stage/act plus callbacks and texture services. Gamma binding resolves the motion-held player allocation, then extra-work references and exact allocation records. Source initializes/overwrites registration arrays in order but retains prior allocation records. Actual native Sonic/Miles/Knuckles/Amy/Big exec callbacks throw, Gamma display/destructor and many lower seams throw, and preview action update throws. Legacy Sonic uses PlayerStartupRegistry in reference code; it is not silently bound to native PlayerSystem.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: Native Gamma units assert actual primary/motion identity, allocation registry lookup, entry current-player null surviving initialization, shared mutable weld pointer, distinct E102WK/cursor allocations and first explicit setup stop. Gate fingerprints the current PlayerSystem header. Gamma original receipt has 1,422 value-exact cases and 498 FP partials; startup receipt is an original prefix stopping before 44297b, not a returned whole callback.
accepted_judges.limits: Consumer contracts only: no native actor playback, destructor cleanup, reentry or full registration/extra-work retirement qualification. Gamma concrete lower receipts are not recovered implementations. Resource-loader/preview holdouts do not close PlayerSystem.

ownership_lifetime_publication_map.contract: LogoScene initialize_heap replaces its arena; following initialize_tasks replaces the scheduler. The old scheduler retains its shared arena until replacement. NativeGame reference reset follows its own explicit initializer boundary; HLE instead performs source CRT/Heap calls and binds guest base/payload transport. These are three composition worlds, not three mutable copies within one world. No source HeapCreate/HeapAlloc success or arbitrary initialization defaults are inferred.

storage_ owns nodes, links borrow. run_index/run_children use WalkGuard; external advance_dispatch users retain cursor/call handles and reconcile between steps. Index order is8,0..6, not0..7. Next and exec are captured before callback; slot reuse resolves new generation, but unreused freed or detached saved-next is tagged failure. Parent/child nested calls do not restore old context: child traversal leaves current_function alone and clears field30 after successful callback; top traversal clears both. SourceTaskFailure preserves partial context; unrelated exceptions follow the explicit cleanup/rethrow path. Empty walks perform no context cleanup.

Display snapshots next/callback, invokes callback, then resolves current slot and reloads child, with execution context unchanged. source_graph carries canonical shared motion/primary/auxiliary handles. restore_source_graph validates complete4096-slot partition, ownership/link traversal/cycles and same-motion-allocation canonical owner before replacement; it reconstitutes task wrapper handles, so callers must resolve slot identities at documented boundaries. A graph snapshot extends shared resource lifetime; it is not a second mutable numeric owner.

ownership_lifetime_publication_map.boundary: Child allocation and live pose copy
ownership_lifetime_publication_map.contract: Source create_child creates detached level7 element first, links/prepends it, then copies position before angles when both primary allocations exist. A canonical parent primary_state requires installed player child factory; no factory is a tagged retained partial failure. The player factory creates the child owner from real zeroed allocation and borrows live parent position/angles; it does not recopy stale arena pose bytes. Native preview currently creates top-level actor tasks rather than proving every live-primary child path.

destroy_task copies requested_task before beginning destruction. A source destructor can reset/replace the canonical handle that was passed by const reference; the active task/callback remains the old allocation. Explicit callbacks retain task/context values. Actual music TitleScene destruction reaches this contract; the registered regression and Main music receipt cover clear and replace. Do not refactor the copy into a reference or reread registry latest after callback.

ownership_lifetime_publication_map.boundary: Source destructor placement and deferred free
ownership_lifetime_publication_map.contract: FreeTask changes exec only. Source destruction invokes destructor, snapshots sibling links, clears callbacks, processes children, unlinks, cleans collision and object chains, then primary/force/motion/auxiliary, then native auxiliary payload, control linkage and recycle. Chain successor is retained before release. Failure retains its exact stage/resources; resume_destruction is native continuation, not a fresh original call. Host retire is separate and rejects source pool tasks. Slot recycle creates a new native task identity; shared handles can retain retired typed state/field30 until dropped. Task retirement must not invent registry/player/animation teardown.

ownership_lifetime_publication_map.boundary: Work allocation generation, interior borrow and unknown bytes
ownership_lifetime_publication_map.contract: Arena live_ owns allocations; references_ is weak. Payload operations permit rounded capacity, including preserved stale bytes, and reject crossing next header. Reference-view offset is attached to an exact allocation identity, not just a numeric pointer; old released handles stay released after offset reuse. Raw write/fill invalidates any overlapping four-byte binding; release removes bindings contained in released payload. Missing reference_base marks only serialized nonnull pointer bytes unavailable; known null writes zero. MetadataWriter transports reference stores, PayloadReader/Writer use live external payload, and resolver is explicit. Failed transports are tagged/retained, not reclassified as game absence.

PInitialize retains Player record in Registry.allocations after512-byte calloc and before parameter consumption. It binds task motion+0 to the exact player allocation, initializes/reuses object work, optionally allocates contact, then publishes task/primary/motion/player registration arrays in that order. Registry overwrite retains the older allocation record. Parameters are content; primary/motion are shared canonical numeric owners. Legacy adapter wraps the same native producer record with availability facts, not another simultaneous native player.

Native Gamma captures motion-held player before initialization, publishes its primary and nullable player, then may register a newly initialized player. Its current player remains the published null; a slot lookup must not refresh it. Sonic publishes through actor_current setters; frozen fixture written bits are separate reference-only receipt state. Null clear, same-value publication and SuperSonic byte173 are legitimate. The three GLOBAL declarations occur once; separate native/reference worlds instantiate the same type and do not create duplicate declarations.

Startup binds player+0x138 to the SAME player allocation interior+0x38 (speed.x), and player+0x13c to same allocation+0 (charge). Actual scalar() consumes reference_view each time and validates exact target then offset; it accepts semantic+0x38/+0, not raw byte-vector speed. Animation owns allocated8-byte action header,12-byte motion header and zeroed111*24 data plus channel keys. Mode0 publishes partial allocations/stores in source order; later cleanup frees keys/data/motion/action and clears reached typed references in order. This is context only for judge8d5eb020: no proof of all malloc-header missingness or alternate alias/failure combinations, no new fixture or playback algorithm.

Session owns scene then PlayerSystem then LogoScene; normal member destruction destroys logo/scheduler before players, and players before scene/pack. PlayerSystem has no custom source actor destructor. Gamma weld rows and cursor templates borrow canonical scene geometry; initialized player joins point to the one gamma_weld member. gamma_work deque push preserves existing element references; lookup checks allocation/released state. Extra580-byte E102WK and expanded cursor buffers are distinct from player auxiliary480 bytes. Current native Gamma destructor/display throw, so explicit free/reentry/erase policy is OPEN. Do not add sweeping RAII frees, duplicate poses or normalize source last-store slots to solve this gap.

Scheduler callback_contexts_ retains explicit per-function owners and rejects conflicting registrations. TitleScene owns a shared CallbackContext with a raw scene borrower; its destructor nulls that borrower, and callback_scene fails if context/scene is absent. Context borrowing is synchronous and cannot be retained as a hidden callback cache. Current Gamma Context task/stage/act/catalog/service references and callback values live only through run(). No global singleton or observer fallback is approved.

absence_and_knownness.meaning: Null task/primary/player/held task/reference or optional allocation failure is a real source value where the producer and consumer establish it; zero/null are not missing fixture data. Absent default_field30 outer optional differs from an engaged empty shared_ptr. Missing reference_base/known bytes, failed payload callback, missing legacy action/field outer optional, or unpublished frozen receipt are observation boundaries, not source nulls. Decoder/importer/reference adapter must preserve lazy read failures and partial stores; no blanket optional ban.

actor_current::Observation is an optional AFTER-store receipt. No observer/empty callback never changes game value or invents missing game state. Each present function observes null/same-value stores. A throwing observer cannot veto the completed store; reentrant observer can affect subsequent live reads.
